result:
No revisit dates have passed. The next one is the bake-to-order review on 2 December 2026.

Here's what I'd try this winter, most promising first:

**1. A subscriber referral offer (start here)**
Each of your 140 subscribers gets a code. A friend who uses it pays half price for their first month, and the subscriber who referred them gets a free pastry or loaf in their next box. You dropped 50% off the first month on 6 October, but the reopen condition you set was "test it with a referral from an existing subscriber." This is that test, so it doesn't reverse the decision. Run it for 6–8 weeks and compare how many referred people keep paying after the first month against the 6 out of 52 from the free box. People invited by a neighbour should stick around much better than strangers chasing a free loaf. If it works, log it as a new decision.

**2. Christmas gift subscriptions**
Sell prepaid 4-week and 8-week bread boxes as gifts, with a printed card, for anyone living within your 3 km area. The recipient never gets anything free, so this fits the no-free-trial rule. December is when people buy gifts, and someone who already likes your bread is a better lead than a free-box taker. In January, invite each recipient to keep their box going.

**3. Winter extras in the box**
Offer a few seasonal bakes as paid add-ons, for example a spiced loaf, a festive pastry or soup bread. They make the subscription more appealing in the months when people stay in, and they raise revenue per box without new customers. Because they're ordered by the 6 pm cutoff, they don't break bake-to-order.

**4. Local outreach for about €300**
Put leaflets in the buildings on your busiest delivery streets ("your neighbours get theirs on Saturday"). Ask 2–3 local offices or co-working spaces within 3 km about a team box. All of this stays inside your own cargo-bike area.

**One thing to check first: Saturday capacity.** The free-box test showed that Saturday slots are your real limit. How many more boxes can you deliver on a Saturday before you're full? If the answer is "not many," a second delivery window (for example Friday evening) may matter more than marketing. A courier won't solve it: you ruled couriers out until you pass 300 subscribers.

I left out free trials and free first boxes. You dropped them on 6 October because only 6 of 52 converted and they used up Saturday slots. That decision only reopens if paid signups stay below 8 a month for two months in a row, and October had 15. Delivery apps and walk-in surplus stock are also out under your existing decisions.

If you commit to any of these, I'll log it in the ledger, including what was dropped.
